Disappointed, expected higher food quality for the price
Jan 2026 • Couples
The restaurant is on the 5th floor of Windsor hotel, so the ambiance is nice and it looks classy and high end. The dim sum quality is a mixed bag. The porridge, chicken feet and fried daikon cake were good, but the soup dumpling and shrimp rice rolls were disappointed considering the higher prices. I was surprised that they charged for 128k VND or ~ $5 USD for a pot of hot tea that only use 1 tea bag. I usually pay $6 USD for a pot of tea at a dim sum place in Northern California that uses real tea leaves.

Disappointing food for such a grand restaurant
Sep 2022 • Family
The ambience is high class Chinese, the servers are trained to be attentive to customers needs, and the rest room was impeccable! 

With the grand entrance I had high hopes for a great dining experience. The rice porrage with an unknown white fish was acceptable with a subtle mild taste but much more was expected. The chicken feet in xo sauce was excellent and highly recommendable. The steamed fillet of grouper was disappointing because of two reasons; one, the fillet tasted like it was previously frozen; and, two, the seasoning was too subtle. 

The mango pudding was exquisite and highly recommendable. This was the best use of a mango in a long time! 

Overall, for the price, the chief needs to up his game to match the ambience and price.

Chinese restaurant to go to in Chinatown
Mar 2020 • Business
Ngan Dinh is situated inside Windsor Plaza Hotel at HCM District 5 (known as Chinatown). This hotel is next to An Duong Plaza, the well known fashion/garment wholesale complex, more suited for locals but its a bargain spree if you know a bit or 2 of Vietnamese.
Ngan Dinh looks and feel like a typical Chaozhou and/or Cantonese restaurant. The head server can converse in Cantonese which makes it easier when ordering. Menu with pictures are also available if you speak neither Vietnamese or Cantonese.
I’ve been coming here on-off for 10 years and its still worth coming to whenever I am around District 5. The mix plater meats are something you must try but overall the dim sums and stir fried dishes are mostly up to mark, hence my return once a while in the last 10 years.
Its a go to place if you are in the district.
